card.summary: The page offers a file-to-link bot that it calls 'fairly enough broken'; no price, quota or daily count is stated.

free_tier.stated: The page offers a file-to-link bot that it calls 'fairly enough broken'; no price, quota or daily count is stated.

per_object_cap.stated: unverified: the bot's page states no per-file cap; Telegram's own file ceiling is 2 GB (4 GB with Premium).

retention.stated: unverified: the bot's page states no storage window or link lifetime.

egress.terms: No traffic allowance or price is stated on the bot's page.

record.interface_detail: A Telegram chat with the bot; the result is a link or a file delivered into the chat. No HTTP API is published.
record.tooling: Any Telegram client; a Telegram account is required to start the bot.
record.chaining: A link to a stored Telegram file; the bot page describes the feature set as broken, so it is a fallback only.

limits.value: 2 GB per file on a free Telegram account (4 GB with Premium); the bot states no cap of its own

record.binding_note: The only number that can be named from evidence is the per-file ceiling; the bot publishes no quota.

identity_cost.detail: A Telegram account, which is logged in with a mobile phone number; no key or card is asked on the bot's page.

record.reliability_note: The bot's page describes its feature set as partly broken.
record.confidence_note: The description is the bot's own, read on its t.me page. Liveness of the backend needs a Telegram account and was not tested. Any paid tier of the bot is unverified: behind a sign-up (it is reached from inside the bot, with a Telegram account); the bot's page states no price.

evidence.quote: A simple enough file to link bot with fairly enough broken features.
evidence.proved: the bot's own page states its offer: A simple enough file to link bot with fairly enough broken features.
